mainTopic: Which objects placed in a window block the spread of טומאת אוהל (reduce the window's size), and the challenges to שמואל's rule that a usable item does not block
overview: The גמרא first finishes a discussion about a barrel stuck in a window. A כלי חרס does not become טמא from its outside, so the גמרא explains that either the barrel's opening faces inward or it is a metal barrel. Then the גמרא brings a ברייתא listing things that reduce a window's size so that טומאה cannot pass through it. It uses this list to challenge שמואל, who holds that anything a person still has a use for, or will remove, does not reduce the window. The גמרא goes through the list item by item: grass, scraps of cloth, a limb dangling from an animal, a bird, a גוי, a בן שמונה, and salt. Each time it asks why the item would not be taken away. Each time it answers by narrowing the case until nothing will remove it, for example a tied, non-kosher, bony bird that scratches, or a government prisoner whom no one dares free. The amud ends with salt resting on a piece of pottery. The גמרא asks why the pottery itself does not do the blocking, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The barrel itself should act as a barrier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the barrel in the window cannot block טומאה, since a כלי חרס does not become טמא from its outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the barrel itself block the טומאה! After all, an earthenware vessel does not become טמא through its outer side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous claim that the barrel in the window does not block the טומאה because it can itself become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that can become טמא cannot serve as a barrier against טומאה. But a כלי חרס only becomes טמא through its inside (its airspace), not from contact on its outside. So if the barrel's back faces the טומאה, it should not become טמא, and it should be able to block.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it serve as a barrier (חציצה) against טומאה
From its back, meaning its outer surface

phrases.english: Let it itself serve as a barrier,
phrases.notes: "It" is the barrel sitting in the window from the earlier discussion.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא כְּלִי חֶרֶשׂ אֵינוֹ מִטַּמֵּא מִגַּבּוֹ!
phrases.english: for an earthenware vessel does not become impure from its back!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the barrel in the window, from before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the barrel does not block because it can become טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כלי חרס cannot become טמא from its outside, so it should not count as something that receives טומאה, and it should block.

steps.title: The barrel's opening faces inward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the barrel's mouth faces into the house, so the טומאה can enter through its opening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where the barrel's opening faces inward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the picture of the case. The barrel is turned so its opening faces inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the opening faces the side of the טומאה, the טומאה enters the barrel's airspace. That is how a כלי חרס does become טמא. Since the barrel can become טמא this way, it cannot act as a barrier.

keyTerms.meaning: The mouth or opening of the vessel

phrases.english: Rather, its opening faces inward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel faced outward, so it could not become טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: The opening faces inward, so it can become טמא and does not block

steps.title: Or it is a metal barrel
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the opening really does face outward, but the barrel is made of metal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say: really its opening faces outward. What case are we dealing with here? A metal barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same challenge. It keeps the barrel facing outward but changes what the barrel is made of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a כלי חרס has the special rule that it becomes טמא only from inside. A metal vessel becomes טמא from its outside too. So a metal barrel can become טמא either way and cannot block.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say this instead (introduces an alternative answer)
What case are we dealing with here?

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי חרס becomes טמא only through its inside, while a metal vessel becomes טמא from its outside too. Either answer explains why the barrel does not block.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
actually, its opening faces outward,
and with what are we dealing here?
With a metal barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel was assumed to be a כלי חרס
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a metal barrel, which becomes טמא from its outside, so it does not block

steps.title: A ברייתא listing what reduces a window's size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא listing items that reduce a window's size and items that do not. It is setting up challenges to שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא. These all reduce the window: grass someone plucked and put in a window, or grass that grew there by itself; scraps of cloth smaller than three by three; a limb or flesh hanging loose from an animal; a bird resting in the window; a גוי sitting in the window; a baby born in the eighth month lying in the window; salt; an earthenware vessel; and a ספר תורה. But snow, hail, frost, ice and water do not reduce the window.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge שמואל's rule. This step sets up the source. The actual challenges come item by item in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A window a טפח by a טפח lets טומאה pass between areas. Something placed in it can shrink the open space below that size (ממעט). שמואל held that an item a person still has a use for does not reduce the window, since it will be removed. Yet the ברייתא lists items that seem usable, like grass and salt, as reducing it.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born in the eighth month, who is not expected to live

steps.confusionAlert: Asking whether an item "reduces" the window is not about whether it touches the טומאה. The question is whether it fills part of the opening, leaving less than a טפח open, so the טומאה cannot pass through.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
grass that one plucked and placed in the window,
or that grew on its own in the windows;

phrases.aramaic: וּמַטְלוֹנִיּוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ;
phrases.english: and cloth scraps that do not measure three by three;
and the limb or the flesh that is dangling
from a domestic animal or a wild animal;
and a bird that rested in the window,
and a gentile who sat in the window,
and an eighth-month baby lying in the window;
and salt, and an earthenware vessel, and a Torah scroll —
all of these reduce the window.
But snow, and hail,
and frost, and ice, and water —
all of these do not reduce the window.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to שמואל's rule from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that an item a person has a use for does not reduce the window
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists items that seem usable, yet says they reduce the window.

steps.title: Grass is food for animals
steps.stepSummary: The first challenge: grass can feed an animal, so by שמואל's rule it should not reduce the window.
steps.simpleTranslation: But grass is fit for his animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the first item in the ברייתא, plucked grass, and uses it to attack שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל's rule, anything a person still has a use for will be taken away, so it does not count as part of the window. Grass can feed animals, so it should not reduce the window. Yet the ברייתא says it does.

phrases.english: But grass is fit for his animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 4 against שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule, applied to the plucked grass in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Grass is usable as animal food, so by שמואל it should not reduce the window, yet the ברייתא says it does.

steps.title: It is poisonous grass
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the ברייתא means אפרזתא, a poisonous grass no animal can eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about אפרזתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a special kind of grass that has no use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אפרזתא is poisonous, so it is not fit for animals. Nobody will take it out of the window, so it stays there and reduces the window. This fits שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A poisonous grass that animals cannot eat

phrases.english: With afrazta.
phrases.notes: A poisonous kind of grass that animals cannot eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ordinary grass that animals eat
steps.terutzMaskana: Poisonous grass with no use, which stays in the window

steps.title: Grass that grows by itself harms the wall
steps.stepSummary: The next challenge: grass growing on its own damages the wall, so the owner will remove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said, "or grass that grew on its own." But since it damages the wall, he will pull it out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case in the ברייתא and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the grass is not food, the owner has a reason to remove it, because its roots harm the wall. Something the owner plans to remove should not count as part of the window. So why does the ברייתא say it reduces the window?

phrases.english: "Or that grew on their own."
Since they damage the wall, he will remove them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that grass growing on its own reduces the window
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner will remove grass that harms his wall, so it should not count as a lasting part of the window.

steps.title: רבה: a ruined wall
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the case is a wall of a ruin, which the owner does not care to protect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is talking about the wall of a ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge by placing the case in a ruined building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one cares about damage to a wall that is already in ruins. So the owner will not bother to pull out the grass. It stays, and it reduces the window.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
With the wall of a ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wall of a lived-in house, which the owner protects
steps.terutzMaskana: A ruined wall, where the grass is left alone

steps.title: רב פפא: grass rooted far from the window
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says it can even be a wall of a lived-in house, where the grass takes root more than three טפחים from the window.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even a wall of a lived-in house. The case is where the grass comes from more than three טפחים away from the window.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different answer that works even for a normal house wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grass is not rooted at the window itself. It grows from a spot more than three טפחים away and stretches over to the window. The owner is not bothered by it there, so he leaves it, and it reduces the window.
steps.whatToRemember: Grass in a window reduces its size only when no one will remove it. That is true when it is poisonous (אפרזתא), when it grows on a ruin (רבה), or when it is rooted more than three טפחים away (רב פפא).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
even with the wall of a settled house,
where they come from beyond three of the window.
phrases.notes: He means three טפחים. The grass is rooted farther away and only reaches over to the window.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּכוֹתֶל יִישּׁוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the challenge in step 7, instead of רבה's
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grass grows at the window and harms the wall there
steps.terutzMaskana: The grass is rooted more than three טפחים away, so the owner does not mind it

steps.title: Scraps of cloth can patch a torn garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's case of rags: they are useful for patching clothes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Scraps of fabric are fit for patching a tear in a garment!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the ברייתא, scraps of fabric, and asks why they shrink the window when they are useful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By שמואל's rule, something useful will be taken away, so it is not treated as part of the wall. Rags can patch a torn garment, so someone will remove them. They should not reduce the window.

phrases.english: Scraps of fabric:
they are fit for patching a tear in a garment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of challenge used on the grass to a new item in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that rags reduce the window.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rags are useful, so by שמואל's rule they will be removed and should not count.

steps.title: The rags are thick
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is thick scraps that are no good for patching.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about thick scraps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means thick rags, which nobody would use to patch clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Narrowing the case to thick rags takes away the use the challenge pointed to. With that use gone, the rags stay in place and count as part of the wall.

phrases.english: With thick ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rags are ordinary fabric that can patch clothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rags are thick and unfit for patching.

steps.title: Thick rags still help a bloodletter
steps.stepSummary: Even thick rags can be used by a bloodletter.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are fit for a bloodletter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: even thick rags have a use, because a bloodletter can wipe blood with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick rags are not good for patching, but they still have another use. So by שמואל's rule they should still be removed.

phrases.english: They are fit for a bloodletter!
phrases.notes: He would use them to wipe up the blood where he made the cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the rags are thick.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thick rags still have a use, so they would still be removed.

steps.title: The rags are rough sackcloth
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is sackcloth, which scratches the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about sackcloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rags are coarse sackcloth, which a bloodletter would not use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sackcloth is too scratchy to wipe a wound. So this use is gone too, and the rags stay in the window.

phrases.english: With sackcloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by narrowing the case further.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thick rags could serve a bloodletter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rags are sackcloth, which is useless for that job.

steps.title: Sackcloth would need a different size
steps.stepSummary: If it is sackcloth, the ברייתא should have given the size for sackcloth, four by four טפחים, not three by three.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is sackcloth, why does it say 'that are not three by three'? It should have said 'that are not four by four'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the sackcloth answer from the ברייתא's own wording about size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the rags as smaller than three by three אצבעות, which is the measure for ordinary clothing fabric. Sackcloth only becomes a real item at four by four טפחים. If the ברייתא meant sackcloth, it would have used that bigger measure.

keyTerms.meaning: three by three (fingerbreadths), the size for clothing fabric
four by four (טפחים), the size for sackcloth

phrases.english: If it is sackcloth,
why does it say 'that are not three by three'?!

phrases.aramaic: ״שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: It should have said 'that are not four by four'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּרִיסַּקָּא, שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13 from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the rags are sackcloth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The size the ברייתא gives fits clothing fabric, not sackcloth.

steps.title: Cloth that is only like sackcloth
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it is regular woven cloth that is stiff like sackcloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is something like sackcloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rags are not real sackcloth. They are woven like clothing but stiff and rough like sackcloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the cloth is woven like clothing, the clothing measure of three by three is correct. Because it is stiff like sackcloth, a bloodletter will not use it. Both problems are solved.
steps.whatToRemember: The rags in the ברייתא are thick, stiff cloth woven like clothing. They are useless for patching and for a bloodletter, so they stay and shrink the window.

phrases.english: Something like sackcloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 and closes the discussion of rags.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rags are real sackcloth, which does not fit the size in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rags are clothing-type fabric that is stiff like sackcloth.

steps.title: A dangling limb: the animal will walk away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says a limb or flesh dangling from an animal shrinks the window, but the animal can get up and leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: A limb or flesh dangling from a domestic or wild animal: the animal gets up and walks away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another item in the ברייתא and asks how a living animal can count as filling the window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that will not stay in place cannot be treated as part of the wall. An animal can simply leave, so its dangling limb should not reduce the window.

keyTerms.meaning: it runs off and goes away

phrases.english: And the limb and the flesh that are dangling
from a domestic animal or a wild animal:
it gets up and goes away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new item in the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling about a dangling limb or flesh.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal will not stay in the window, so it cannot count as closing it.

steps.title: The animal is tied
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the animal is tied in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a tied animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the animal is tied up, so it cannot leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the animal is tied, it stays where it is, so the dangling part can fill the window.

phrases.english: With a tied one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal is free to walk off.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal is tied and stays in place.

steps.title: The owner will slaughter it
steps.stepSummary: Even a tied animal will be taken away to be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will slaughter it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: the owner will take the animal and slaughter it, so it will not stay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being tied stops the animal from leaving on its own. But the owner has a reason to move it, so it is still not lasting.

phrases.english: He will slaughter it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the animal is tied.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner will remove the animal to slaughter it.

steps.title: The animal is not kosher
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it is a non-kosher animal, which is not slaughtered for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a non-kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the animal is טמאה, so nobody will slaughter it to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal cannot be eaten, so the reason to slaughter it is gone.

phrases.english: With a non-kosher one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal could be slaughtered for food.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is non-kosher, so it will not be slaughtered.

steps.title: The owner will sell it to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: Even a non-kosher animal can be sold to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will sell it to a non-Jew!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again: the owner can sell the non-kosher animal to a גוי, and then it will be taken away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher animal still has value, because a גוי may eat it. So the owner still has a reason to move it.

phrases.english: He will sell it to a non-Jew!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the animal is non-kosher.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It can still be sold, so it will be removed.

steps.title: The animal is too thin to sell
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it is a scrawny animal nobody will buy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a lean animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the animal is so thin that no one would buy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no buyer, the owner has no reason to sell it, so it stays where it is.

phrases.english: With a lean one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal could be sold to a גוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is too thin for anyone to buy.

steps.title: He will cut off the piece for the dogs
steps.stepSummary: Even if the animal stays, the owner can cut off the dangling piece and feed it to dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will cut it off and throw it to the dogs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges once more. The animal may stay, but the dangling piece itself is useful as dog food, so it will be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the questions were about the whole animal leaving. Now the challenge is about the dangling piece alone: it has a use, so by שמואל's rule it should not count.

phrases.english: He will cut it off and throw it to the dogs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 21 from a new angle: the dangling piece itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the dangling limb stays in place.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The piece is useful as dog food, so it will be cut off and removed.

steps.title: He will not cut it because it would hurt the animal
steps.stepSummary: The answer: cutting it would cause צער בעלי חיים, so he will not do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there is suffering to the animal, he will not do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the owner will not cut off the piece, because that would cause the animal pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern for צער בעלי חיים holds the owner back from cutting off the piece. So the limb stays, and the ברייתא's ruling that it reduces the window stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The dangling limb counts as filling the window only in a narrow case: the animal is tied, non-kosher, and too thin to sell. The owner also will not cut off the piece because of צער בעלי חיים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא assumes people avoid causing an animal pain, and it uses that assumption to decide what will realistically stay in place.

phrases.english: Since there is suffering to the animal,
he will not do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים, לָא עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 and closes the discussion of the dangling limb.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining human behavior (a reason the owner will not act)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner would cut off the useful piece for the dogs.
steps.terutzMaskana: He will not cut it off, because that would cause the animal suffering.

steps.title: A bird resting in the window
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the ברייתא: a bird that rests in the window makes the window count as smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a bird that rests in the window (also reduces its size).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the next case from the ברייתא's list. This sets up a new round of questions, just like the ones about the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something in a window only reduces its size if it is going to stay there. A bird seems likely to leave, so this line invites the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Window, an opening in a wall

phrases.english: And a bird that rests in the window.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the animal case to the next item in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird resting in a window reduces the window's size.

steps.title: But the bird will fly away
steps.stepSummary: A bird will just fly off, so how can it count as part of the window?
steps.simpleTranslation: It will fly and leave!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: a bird does not stay put.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only something that stays can reduce the window. A bird is temporary, so it should not count.

phrases.english: It will fly and go away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the bird case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's bird case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bird is not permanent, so it cannot reduce the window.

steps.title: The bird is tied
steps.stepSummary: The case is a bird that is tied in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a tied bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bird is tied down, so it cannot fly away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tying the bird removes the worry that it will fly off.

phrases.english: It is talking about a tied bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird is free to fly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bird is tied, so it stays.

steps.title: But the owner will slaughter it
steps.stepSummary: Even a tied bird might be taken down and slaughtered for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will slaughter it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again: the owner will take the bird and slaughter it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being tied does not keep it there forever if the owner plans to eat it.

phrases.english: He will slaughter it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The tied-bird answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner will remove it to eat it.

steps.title: The bird is non-kosher
steps.stepSummary: It is a non-kosher bird, which nobody slaughters for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a non-kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bird is טמא, so the owner will not slaughter it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher bird cannot be eaten, so the reason to remove it is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Non-kosher (here, a bird that may not be eaten)

phrases.english: It is talking about a non-kosher bird.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27, the same way step 19 answered for the animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird is kosher and will be eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is non-kosher, so it will not be slaughtered.

steps.title: But he can sell it to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: Even a non-kosher bird can be sold to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will sell it to a גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: the owner will sell it to a גוי, who may eat it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher bird still has value, so it may still be taken away.

phrases.english: He will sell it to a non-Jew!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 28, like step 20 did for the animal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The non-kosher answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It can still be sold and removed.

steps.title: It is a bony קלניתא
steps.stepSummary: It is a קלניתא, a bird so bony nobody would buy it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קלניתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is a kind of bird so skinny that no one wants to buy it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no buyer, the owner has no reason to take it down.

keyTerms.meaning: A very bony bird that nobody buys to eat

phrases.english: It is talking about a קלניתא.
phrases.notes: A bird with almost no meat on it, so nobody would pay for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29, like step 21 for the animal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird is worth selling.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a worthless, bony bird.

steps.title: But he can give it to a child
steps.stepSummary: Even a worthless bird could be given to a child to play with.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will give it to a child!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: the owner can hand the bird to a child as a toy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without food value, the bird has a use, so it may still be taken away.

phrases.english: He will give it to a child!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The קלניתא answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It can still be removed as a child's plaything.

steps.title: The bird scratches
steps.stepSummary: It is a bird that scratches, so nobody gives it to a child.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a bird that scratches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bird scratches, so it is too dangerous to give to a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scratching bird is no toy, so the last reason to remove it is gone.

phrases.english: It is talking about one that scratches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bird is safe for a child.
steps.terutzMaskana: It scratches, so no one will give it to a child.

steps.title: But a קלניתא does not scratch
steps.stepSummary: The two answers clash: a קלניתא is not a scratching bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קלניתא does not scratch!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last two answers do not fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 30 said the bird is a קלניתא, and step 32 said it scratches. But a קלניתא is known not to scratch, so both cannot be true.

phrases.english: A קלניתא does not scratch!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 32 contradicts step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The combination of the קלניתא and scratching answers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two descriptions cannot be true of the same bird.

steps.title: A bird like a קלניתא
steps.stepSummary: It is a bird similar to a קלניתא: bony, but it does scratch.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a bird like a קלניתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the bird is not actually a קלניתא but a similar kind of bird, bony like it, that also scratches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps both conditions: nobody buys it because it is bony, and nobody gives it to a child because it scratches. So it will truly stay in the window.
steps.whatToRemember: A bird reduces the window only if nothing will remove it: it is tied, non-kosher, too bony to sell, and too scratchy to give a child.

phrases.english: It is talking about one like a קלניתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 and closes the bird case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is an actual קלניתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a similar bird that is bony and scratches.

steps.title: A גוי sitting in the window
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's next item: a גוי sitting in the window reduces its size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a גוי who sits in the window (reduces its size).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case from the ברייתא. This sets up another round of questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can obviously get up and leave, so the גמרא will need to explain how this counts as staying.

phrases.english: And a non-Jew who sits in the window.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי sitting in a window reduces the window's size.

steps.title: But he will get up and leave
steps.stepSummary: A person will just stand up and walk away.
steps.simpleTranslation: He will get up and go!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: the גוי is not going to stay in the window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, only something that stays counts.

phrases.english: He will stand up and go away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גוי case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person will not stay.

steps.title: He is tied up
steps.stepSummary: The case is a גוי who is tied up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is tied up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he is bound, so he cannot leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being bound keeps him in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Bound, tied up (said of a person)

phrases.english: It is talking about one who is tied up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 36.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He is free to leave.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is tied up.

steps.title: But a friend will untie him
steps.stepSummary: Another person will come and untie him.
steps.simpleTranslation: His friend will come and untie him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: someone else will come and set him free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being tied is not permanent if others can release him.

phrases.english: His friend will come and untie him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The tied-up answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone else will release him.

steps.title: He is a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: He is a מצורע, so people stay away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the man is a מצורע, so nobody will come near to untie him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People avoid touching a מצורע, so he will stay tied.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, a skin disease people keep away from

phrases.english: It is talking about a מצורע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 38.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone would untie him.
steps.terutzMaskana: People avoid a מצורע.

steps.title: But another מצורע will untie him
steps.stepSummary: A fellow מצורע is not afraid and will untie him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another מצורע, his friend, will come and untie him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: another מצורע has no reason to keep away and will free him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear of touching a מצורע does not apply to someone who already has צרעת.

phrases.english: Another מצורע, his friend, will come and untie him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The מצורע answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fellow מצורע would not keep away.

steps.title: A prisoner of the king
steps.stepSummary: Dropping the מצורע answer, the גמרא says he is a prisoner held by the government.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is talking about prisoners of the king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the מצורע answer and gives a new one: he is held by the government, so nobody dares free him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows the earlier answer is set aside. Fear of the government stops everyone, sick or healthy, from untying him, so he truly stays.
steps.whatToRemember: A גוי reduces the window only if he truly cannot leave: he is a prisoner of the government whom no one dares release.

phrases.english: Rather, it is talking about prisoners of the king.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 40 and replaces the מצורע answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He stays because he is a מצורע.
steps.terutzMaskana: He stays because nobody dares free a government prisoner.

steps.title: A בן שמונה placed in the window
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's next item: a baby born in the eighth month, placed in the window, reduces its size.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a baby born in the eighth month who is placed in the window (reduces its size).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next case. This sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בן שמונה is a baby born after only eight months, who was considered unable to survive. The question will again be whether he stays in the window.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born in the eighth month, considered unable to live

phrases.english: And an eight-month baby who is placed in the window.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next item in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן שמונה lying in a window reduces the window's size.

steps.title: But his mother will pick him up
steps.stepSummary: The mother will come and take the baby away.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mother will come and pick him up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: a mother will surely remove her baby from the window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the baby will be moved, he is not permanent and should not reduce the window.

phrases.english: His mother will come and pick him up!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 42.
steps.kashyaTarget: The בן שמונה case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The mother will remove the baby.

steps.title: It is on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The case is on שבת, when the mother may not move him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case happens on שבת, when moving this baby is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she is not allowed to pick him up, he will stay in the window. The next step brings the source showing he may not be moved.

phrases.english: It is talking about שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 43.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother can move him any day.
steps.terutzMaskana: On שבת she may not move him.

steps.title: A בן שמונה is like a stone on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בן שמונה is like a stone and may not be moved on שבת, though his mother may bend over him to nurse.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A baby born in the eighth month is like a stone, and it is forbidden to move him on שבת. But his mother bends over him and nurses him, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that a בן שמונה may not be moved on שבת. So the mother will leave him in the window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he cannot survive, he is treated like a stone, which is מוקצה and may not be moved. She may still lean over and nurse him because of danger, but she does not pick him up, so he stays put.
steps.confusionAlert: Nursing is allowed, but she still may not lift him. She bends over him where he lies, which is why he stays in the window.
steps.whatToRemember: A בן שמונה reduces the window on שבת, because he is like a stone and may not be moved, even by his mother.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a שבת law about moving things can decide a question about טומאה: what may not be moved counts as staying in place.

phrases.english: As it is taught: an eight-month baby
is like a stone,
phrases.notes: Since he cannot live, he is treated like a stone, which is מוקצה and may not be moved on שבת.

phrases.english: and it is forbidden to move him on שבת.
But his mother bends over him and nurses him,
because of the danger.
phrases.notes: The danger is to the mother, who could become ill if she does not nurse.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: בֶּן שְׁמֹנֶה הֲרֵי הוּא כְּאֶבֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 44 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a בן שמונה may not be moved on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: בן שמונה הרי הוא כאבן ואסור לטלטלו בשבת

steps.title: Salt is useful, so someone will take it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's next item is salt. The גמרא objects that salt is useful, so people will remove it from the window.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says salt shrinks the window. But salt is useful, so someone will take it away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next item on the ברייתא's list, salt, and immediately challenges it. Salt is a useful thing, so it will not stay in the window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object only shrinks a window if it is left there for good. Salt is something people use, so by שמואל's rule it should not count. This is the same 'it is fit for use' challenge the גמרא raised about the grass (step 5) and the rags (step 10).

keyTerms.meaning: It is fit for him (it is useful), so he will use it

phrases.english: Salt (reduces the window)? It is fit for him to use!
phrases.notes: The word מֶלַח is the ברייתא's item. The rest is the גמרא's objection: he will take it for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next item in the ברייתא's list (salt) and applies the same 'it is fit for use' challenge used on the grass and rags.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that salt shrinks a window
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A useful object will be taken away, so it is not left there for good and should not count.

steps.title: It is bitter salt
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means bitter salt, which is not used for food.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about bitter salt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means bitter salt, which nobody wants for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is narrowed so that the salt has no food use. Without a use, nobody will bother taking it, so it stays in the window.

phrases.english: With bitter salt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Salt is useful and will be taken away.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bitter salt is not used as food, so it stays.

steps.title: Bitter salt is still good for hides
steps.stepSummary: Even bitter salt is used for tanning hides, so someone will still take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is useful for hides!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. Bitter salt may be useless for food, but it is still used for working hides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer only removed one use of the salt. Another use remains, so the salt will still be taken away.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal hides (salt is used to tan them)

phrases.english: It is fit for hides!
phrases.notes: Salt was used in preparing and tanning leather.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the bitter-salt answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא means bitter salt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bitter salt still has a use, tanning, so it will be removed.

steps.title: The salt has thorns in it
steps.stepSummary: The salt is mixed with thorns, so it is no good for hides either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The salt has thorns in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the case again. This salt has thorns mixed in, which would ruin hides, so nobody will use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the salt is useless for food and also for tanning. With no use left, it will stay in the window.

phrases.english: That has thorns in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the hides challenge by narrowing the case further.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bitter salt is still used for hides.
steps.terutzMaskana: Salt with thorns is useless for hides as well.

steps.title: Salt damages the wall, so he will remove it
steps.stepSummary: Even useless salt will be cleared away, because salt damages the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since salt is bad for the wall, he will take it away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new kind of reason to remove the salt. The owner wants it gone because it harms his wall, even if he has no use for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier challenges were about wanting the salt. This one is about wanting to get rid of it. Either way it will not stay, so it should not count.

phrases.english: Since it is harmful to the wall, he will remove it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that the salt is useless but finds a different reason it will be removed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The thorny, bitter salt case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Salt eats away at the wall, so the owner will clear it out, and it is not left there for good.

steps.title: The salt sits on a piece of pottery
steps.stepSummary: The salt rests on a piece of pottery, so it does not touch or damage the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is sitting on a piece of pottery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the salt sits on a piece of broken pottery. The wall is protected, so there is no reason to remove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pottery keeps the salt away from the wall. Now the salt has no use and does no harm, so it stays.

phrases.english: That it sits on a shard of pottery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wall-damage challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The salt damages the wall and will be removed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sitting on pottery, the salt does not touch the wall.

steps.title: Then let the pottery itself shrink the window
steps.stepSummary: If there is pottery in the window, the pottery should count, so why does the ברייתא mention salt?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the piece of pottery itself be the thing that blocks!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own last answer. If a piece of pottery is sitting in the window, the pottery already shrinks it, so there is nothing new in listing salt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists salt as its own item, which implies the salt is what does the shrinking. If the pottery already blocks the space, the salt adds nothing. The גמרא answers this on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it block (serve as a barrier)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about whether the salt stays put. It asks why the ברייתא needs salt at all, since the pottery should already do the job.

phrases.english: Let the shard itself serve as a barrier!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the pottery answer into a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the salt sits on pottery
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If pottery is there, it already shrinks the window, so the ברייתא's mention of salt teaches nothing.
